rationale: Both responses propose similar multi-signal scoring classifiers covering temporal and volatility behaviour, schema density, FK fan-in and fan-out, entropy and naming semantics. Both use a review band for ambiguous cases, calibration on labelled tables, SCD handling and periodic re-scoring. B has nice touches: distinct-value ratios, near-uniqueness of descriptive combinations, metadata-only computation, and a pseudocode skeleton. However, B inverts its headline 'strongest' signal: it says the insert-to-update ratio is high for master data and low for transactional data, when append-heavy transactional tables have the higher ratio. A gets this right, and adds other well-reasoned discriminators: the volume ratio to the referenced master table, delete ratio, record age and CV of daily deltas. A also has a cold-start fallback for tables without history. A has minor questionable claims, such as entropy direction and a muddled SCD note. Even so, its core calculations are sound and better specified, which makes it the more reliable design.
